newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ equities close higher as debt market rallies.
newsitem.headline: NZ equities close higher as debt market rallies.

text.p: * Rally in debt market boosts equities
* Interest rate fall not seen fully priced in to equities
* Strong interest in Fletcher Building, Fletcher Paper
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
333 +5 * NZSC cap index +12.89 at 4,957.82
355 -4 * Volume NZ$51.6 million. Futures +5 at 1,190
744 -1 * Other movers - +15 +10
The New Zealand share market again finished higher on Tuesday, powered by the second consecutive day's rally in the debt market.
Brokers said equities have not yet fully priced in the fall in rates and the market could run further.

"These declining interest rates are fuelling equities. The feeling of the market is good and we don't think the equities market has priced in declines in interest rates over the last 10 days. We think there is more to go," said Don Turkington of Cavill White Securities.
The top 40 index gained 11.02 to 2,378.91 on volume of $51.6 million.

Star of the day was Fletcher Paper, which gained 12 cents to $2.67. Brokers said investors are taking a counter cyclical view of the pulp industry, estimating that pulp prices were at, or near, the bottom of the cycle.
Fellow forestry stock Carter Holt Harvey also had a good day, gaining five cents to $3.33.
Fletcher Building, seen as a beneficiary of increased government spending, gained four cents to $4.14.
Telecom ended down one cent to $7.44, but Turkington believes that with a gross return of eight percent it was one stock likely to shine in a lower interest rate environment.
Cavalier gained six cents to $3.17, and was also seen one to gain from the lower interest rates.
Turkington said a Privy Council ruling against Inland Revenue on the Rangatira case, seen as a test on the taxation of profits from share trading, would be positive for equities.
